sections.title: Accounting Rules
sections.description: The golden rules of double entry.

items.title: Golden rules (traditional)
items.body: Real accounts: Debit what comes in, Credit what goes out. Personal accounts: Debit the receiver, Credit the giver. Nominal accounts: Debit expenses and losses, Credit incomes and gains.

items.title: Modern rule
items.body: Assets and expenses increase on the debit side; liabilities, capital and income increase on the credit side. Every transaction has equal debits and credits.

items.title: Fundamental concepts
items.body: Business entity, going concern, accrual, consistency, prudence, materiality and matching — the assumptions that keep accounting consistent and comparable.

sections.title: Journal Rules
sections.description: How to write a correct journal entry.

items.title: Format
items.body: Date first, then the account(s) debited, then the account(s) credited (indented, prefixed 'To'), amounts in two columns, and a narration explaining the transaction.

items.title: Balancing
items.body: Total debits must equal total credits. Compound entries may carry several debits or credits.

items.title: Common entries
items.body: Cash sale: Dr Cash / Cr Sales. Credit purchase: Dr Purchases / Cr Supplier. Payment to supplier: Dr Supplier / Cr Bank. Depreciation: Dr Depreciation Expense / Cr Accumulated Depreciation.

sections.title: Key Formulas
sections.description: The formulas used throughout the curriculum.

items.title: Accounting equation
items.body: Assets = Liabilities + Capital.

items.title: Cost of goods sold
items.body: Opening stock + purchases - closing stock.

items.title: Gross profit
items.body: Sales - cost of goods sold.

items.title: Straight-line depreciation
items.body: (Cost - residual value) ÷ useful life.

items.title: Reducing-balance depreciation
items.body: Fixed % of the written-down value each year.

items.title: Cash from operations (indirect)
items.body: Net profit + non-cash items - increase in current assets + increase in current liabilities.

items.title: GST payable
items.body: Output GST - input GST (set off and remit the difference).

sections.title: Ratios
sections.description: The ratios used in financial statement analysis.

items.title: Current ratio
items.body: Current assets ÷ current liabilities. A common benchmark is 2:1.

items.title: Quick (acid-test) ratio
items.body: (Current assets - inventory) ÷ current liabilities. A benchmark near 1:1.

items.title: Debt-equity ratio
items.body: Total debt ÷ shareholders' funds. Measures financial leverage.

items.title: Gross margin
items.body: Gross profit ÷ sales.

items.title: Net margin
items.body: Net profit ÷ sales.

items.title: ROCE
items.body: Operating profit ÷ capital employed.

items.title: Inventory turnover
items.body: Cost of goods sold ÷ average inventory.

items.title: Receivables days
items.body: Average receivables ÷ credit sales × 365.

items.title: P&L vs balance sheet
items.body: The P&L covers a period (performance); the balance sheet is a snapshot at a date (position). Net profit flows from the P&L into capital in the balance sheet.

items.title: Accruals and prepayments
items.body: Outstanding expenses are added to the P&L expense and shown as a liability. Prepayments are deducted and shown as an asset.

items.title: Closing stock
items.body: Appears on the credit side of the trading account (reduces COGS) and as a current asset.

items.title: Profit is not cash
items.body: Credit sales and inventory build-up create profit without cash. Always read the P&L with the cash flow statement.

items.title: Three sections
items.body: Operating (core business), investing (long-term assets), financing (capital, loans, dividends).

items.title: Indirect method
items.body: Start with net profit, add back non-cash items (depreciation), deduct increases in current assets, add increases in current liabilities.

items.title: Direct method
items.body: Cash received from customers minus cash paid to suppliers and employees — simpler to understand, harder to compile.

items.title: Output GST
items.body: GST collected on sales — a liability until remitted. Sales are recorded net of GST.

items.title: Input GST
items.body: GST paid on purchases — a receivable from the government until set off.

items.title: Set-off and remittance
items.body: Set input GST against output GST; remit the net difference within the due date.

items.title: Deduction
items.body: Deduct tax at source on specified payments (salaries, rent, professional fees) and deposit it with the government.

items.title: Entries
items.body: Debit the full expense; credit TDS Payable and the net to bank. TDS is the payee's tax collected in advance — not the payer's expense.

items.title: The consolidation process
items.body: Combine line items, eliminate the investment against the subsidiary's equity, remove intra-group balances and transactions, and recognise non-controlling interests.

items.title: Unrealised profit
items.body: Profit on intra-group transfers of inventory still held within the group is eliminated until the goods are sold to outsiders.

items.title: Goodwill
items.body: Consideration + NCI - identifiable net assets at fair value. Tested for impairment annually, never amortised.

items.title: Substance over form
items.body: Report the economic reality of a transaction, not merely its legal form.

items.title: Revenue (Ind AS 115)
items.body: Five-step model: contract, performance obligations, transaction price, allocation, recognition over time or at a point in time.

items.title: Leases (Ind AS 116)
items.body: Lessees recognise right-of-use assets and lease liabilities for virtually all leases.

items.title: Deferred tax (Ind AS 12)
items.body: Recognise deferred tax on temporary differences between carrying amount and tax base.

items.title: Goodwill (Ind AS 36)
items.body: Impairment-only approach; goodwill is never amortised.
